Leiomyoma: The patient's symptoms and histological examination results are consistent with leiomyoma, a smooth muscle tumor. The presence of spindle-shaped cells, strong reactivity against smooth muscle actin (SMA), and negative reaction against S-100 and epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) support this diagnosis.

The presence of spindle-shaped cells arranged in fascicles with cigar-shaped nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm, along with strong reactivity against smooth muscle actin (SMA), supports the diagnosis of Leiomyoma. The clinical presentation of a volarly placed soft tissue mass with well-defined margins and an ovoid shape, in direct contact with the flexor tendons, is also consistent with this diagnosis.
Nerve Sheath Tumor: Although the patient presents with sensory loss in the median nerve distribution and a positive Tinel's sign, the histological examination does not support the diagnosis of Nerve Sheath Tumor, as it lacks S-100 positivity and schwannian differentiation.
